sentences.text: Isanodus, which translates to "Isan Tooth," was an extinct freshwater shark.
This animal belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, the group containing all sharks and rays.
Scientists currently recognize two distinct species within this genus: Isanodus paladeji and Isanodus nongbualamphuensis.
The genus was first described by Cuny and colleagues in the year 2006.
The species Isanodus paladeji serves as the type species, acting as the name-bearing example for the genus.
To date, the Paleobiology Database records three specific fossil occurrences of this animal.
The parent group for Isanodus is the family Lonchidiidae.
Consequently, Isanodus is formally classified within the family Lonchidiidae.
Taxonomists note that Isanodus is closely related to the genus Heteroptychodus.
These sharks lived during the Barremian stage, a time period spanning from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
Fossil remains have been discovered in the Lower Cretaceous deposits of Phu Phan Thong Locality in Nong Bua Lam Phu, Thailand.
